claim: Official 2026 Linux requirements: Dropbox folder must sit on ext4, zfs, eCryptFS (backed by ext4), xfs or btrfs; LAN sync is IPv4-only; ARM unsupported.
quote: A Dropbox folder on a hard drive or partition, formatted with one of the following system types: ext4, zfs, eCryptFS (back by ext4), xfs, btrfs

claim: One on-disk Dropbox folder cannot be shared between Windows and Linux installs because the clients have no supported filesystem in common.
quote: Dropbox for Linux refuses to write to an NTFS partition, and similarly Dropbox for Windows refuses to write to ext4.

claim: The Dropbox desktop client can corrupt git repositories; git-remote-dropbox uses the API directly instead of the desktop client.
quote: The desktop client is not aware of how Git manages it's on-disk format, so if there are concurrent changes or delays in syncing, it's possible to have conflicts that result in a corrupted Git repository.

claim: Maestral, the leading open-source Dropbox client for Linux/macOS, was archived on 2026-07-28.
quote: As of 2026-07-28, this project is archived. It's been a fun challenge to develop a syncing client, but unfortunately, I find too little time to invest in Maestral these days.

claim: Dropbox announced in August 2018 that from 7 November 2018 only ext4 would be supported on Linux.
quote: Starting on November 7th 2018, Dropbox announced that only the ext4 file system would be supported in Linux for synchronizing folders in the Dropbox desktop app.

claim: The filesystem restriction exists because Dropbox stores file identity in extended attributes.
quote: Dropbox uses extended attributes (X-attrs) to identify files in their folder and to keep them in sync.

claim: Dropbox restored zfs and xfs (64-bit) plus btrfs and eCryptFS in beta build 77.3.127, July 2019.
quote: Dropbox brought back support for ZFS and XFS on 64-bit Linux systems, and Btrfs and eCryptFS on all Linux systems in its Beta Build 77.3.127.

claim: dropbox-filesystem-fix is an LD_PRELOAD shim patching the client's filesystem detection; archived November 2025, tested only to client 89.4.278.
quote: I have stopped using the official Dropbox Linux client, so this project is in maintenance mode, and it will not receive any more patches from me.

claim: Deleting a file inside a shared folder removes it for every member, not just locally.
quote: If you delete a file inside a shared folder (without permanently deleting it), that file disappears from the shared folder for everyone, not just you.

claim: Dropbox keeps deleted files and prior versions for 30-365 days depending on plan, and Rewind can undo mass deletions.
quote: Dropbox keeps your deleted files and edits for up to 1 year, depending on your plan.

claim: Smart Sync / online-only files are documented for Windows and Mac only, not Linux.
quote: The system requirements for using online-only files are: Windows: 7 and higher. Mac: OS 10.12 and higher.

claim: Online-only files on Linux is a long-standing user request with no Dropbox commitment.
quote: Smart Sync is only available on Windows and Mac. Dropbox has made no announcement on its availability on Linux.

claim: Selective sync is per-device and folder-granular; individual files cannot be selected.
quote: The selective sync preferences you choose are unique to each computer and don't affect other computers you use with Dropbox.

claim: Linux ignore uses the com.dropbox.ignored xattr per file/folder, is not pattern-based, needs the default Dropbox folder location, and removes the content from the server and other devices.
quote: attr -s com.dropbox.ignored -V 1 '/home/yourname/Dropbox (Personal)/YourFileName.pdf'

claim: The Linux CLI ships help, start, autostart, proxy, lansync, throttle, running, status, filestatus, ls, sharelink, stop and exclude.
quote: exclude - Manages selective sync by displaying, adding, or removing directories from synchronization

claim: File-manager integration on Linux is provided only by the official nautilus-dropbox extension, which builds against GTK4 Nautilus.
quote: Dropbox Integration for Nautilus

claim: Headless Linux use runs the tarball's ~/.dropbox-dist/dropboxd and links the account via a pasted URL, controlled by dropbox.py.
quote: wget -O - "https://www.dropbox.com/download?plat=lnx.x86" | tar xzf - followed by ~/.dropbox-dist/dropboxd

claim: The Linux desktop app requires GTK 2.24, GDK 2.24, Glib 2.40 and LibAppIndicator 12.10; only Ubuntu 18.04+ and Fedora 28+ are supported; LXDE cannot be supported. Page updated 9 Feb 2026.
quote: The Dropbox desktop app for Linux is changing.

claim: A shared folder counts against every member's quota unless all members share a Standard/Advanced/Enterprise team or Family plan.
quote: The size of a shared folder will be counted against the quota of every member of that folder, unless each person is on the same Dropbox Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise team or Dropbox Family plan.

claim: Conflicted copies arise from simultaneous edits, offline edits, or a file left open in an auto-saving app on another machine.
quote: Two users change the same file at the same time. Someone edits a file offline while someone else edits the same file. A file is left open on another user's computer, which Dropbox saves as a new edit.

claim: Dropbox Basic allows only three linked devices at a time; a dual-boot machine consumes two slots.
quote: Dropbox Basic lets you sign in to a maximum of three devices at a time.

claim: Symlinks pointing outside the Dropbox folder sync as link files only; Windows Dropbox does not support symlinks or junctions at all.
quote: symlinks are synced as individual symlink files, and don't sync the files referenced by the symlink if they're outside of your Dropbox folder.

claim: Case-only-differing names created on Linux get mangled by Dropbox because the namespace behaves case-insensitively across platforms.
quote: When Dropbox senses two files or directories with the same name but different cases, it mungs them.

claim: rclone's Dropbox backend documents case-insensitivity, restricted filenames, mtime-only-on-reupload, a 10000-file purge limit, and --dropbox-shared-folders for shared folders.
quote: Dropbox is case insensitive so you can't have a file called "Hello.doc" and one called "hello.doc".

claim: Sync daemons consume one inotify watch per directory; the historic default is 8192, Dropbox recommends 100000, and kernels 5.11+ auto-scale to 1048576.
quote: Dropbox support recommends an inotify.max_user_watches value of 100000

claim: Maestral is unmaintained as of June 2026 and will only work until its certificates expire; it offers selective sync, .mignore gitignore patterns and no device cap.
quote: As of June 2026, Maestral is no longer actively maintained.

claim: Maestral syncs shared folders but cannot manage Dropbox Paper, teams, or shared-folder settings.
quote: Maestral currently does not support Dropbox Paper, the management of Dropbox teams, and the management of shared folder settings.

claim: rclone bisync is explicitly flagged as advanced with data-loss risk if the limitations are not understood.
quote: Bisync is considered an advanced command, so use with care. Make sure you have read and understood the entire manual (especially the Limitations section) before using, or data loss can result.

claim: Syncthing is peer-to-peer with no central server, so it cannot participate in a Dropbox shared folder.
quote: none of your data is ever stored anywhere else other than on your computers. There is no central server that might be compromised.

claim: dbxfs mounts a Dropbox account as a FUSE filesystem, the only Linux route to online-only access; current version 2.0.1, Python 3.11+, GPLv3.
quote: dbxfs allows you to mount your Dropbox folder as if it were a local file system.

claim: The dbxfs GitHub repository was archived in July 2021 and development moved off GitHub.
quote: User-space file system for Dropbox

claim: Insync Desktop is a one-time $39.99 per cloud account with unlimited machines; the Server plan is $159.99/year per machine.
quote: One-time payment: $39.99 per cloud account ... Unlimited machines

claim: Insync is a commercial Linux client supporting Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox including Dropbox team folders.
quote: Insync supports Google Drive, OneDrive, Sharepoint and Dropbox with advanced local sync features.

claim: Dropbox rejects the characters \ / : * ? " < > | and names beyond roughly 255 characters including path.
quote: The special characters you can't use for file naming include \ / : * ? " < > |
